notes.title: Development Newsletter: September Development Updates
notes.content:
[p]Hello all! [/p][h3]
[b]It is once again time to share some updates regarding the game’s development! [/b][/h3][p] For the past several weeks I have been hard at work focusing on issues and fixes for the upcoming game demo. The open playtest has so far been very successful, and I want to extend a huge thanks to everyone that livestreamed or posted recorded footage of the playtest online and/or provided bug reports and other feedback through the online reporting form.[/p][p]The feedback I received led to a large number of bug fixes and improvements for the upcoming Game Demo.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/8e10cf8e25b3e7ddef00239b351d152e0017cd69.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Playtest Data[/b][/h3][p]So far over 300 people have requested access to the playtest, and approximately one third of those that requested access downloaded and played through the game.[/p][p]The average playtime was a whopping [b]1 Hour 51 Minutes [/b]– quite a long average for a game demo – with some users even providing more than 5 hours of recorded footage with which I’ve been able to make substantial bug fixes and improvements.[/p][h3]
[b]Game Updates During the Open Beta[/b][/h3][p]Game updates during this period have primarily been bug fixes - although one new area (Hillside Camp near Gravenstaad) was also added as a location that can be discovered after dying in certain areas of the map.[/p][p]The recent updates also include a lot of quality-of-life improvements as well such as:[/p][list][*][p]Clearer inventory UI with item descriptions for items in all containers[/p][/*][*][p]A shortcut for quick-saving the game[/p][/*][*][p]Improved accessibility options including a new sound setting for weather-related SFX and a mouse sensitivity setting[/p][/*][*][p]Various improvements to the crafting UI and crafter behaviour[/p][/*][*][p]Improved combat difficulty settings[/p][/*][*][p]Better food stacking and food availability during the tutorial[/p][/*][*][p]Clearer notifications and gameplay instructions during the tutorial[/p][/*][*][p]Easier boss area at the end of the tutorial[/p][/*][/list][p]A full record of changes are available from the Notes on the Hermit Playtest community page: [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/3970160"]https://steamcommunity.com/app/3970160[/url][/p][p] [/p][h3][b]What’s Next?[/b][/h3][p]The open Beta period for the Hermit Demo will still remain accessible for a few more days. Some time next week, however, the open playtest period will end and the [b]game demo will be offline for a brief period.[/b] We’ll then be on our way to releasing the game demo on the actual demo page sometime near the end of September/early October.  [/p][p]While I do plan on continuing to address bugs and issues in the demo for some time, the main focus will shift back to the main game development so that the final product can hopefully be completed some time early-mid 2026.[/p][h3][/h3][h3][b]Thank you for your continued support of the project![/b][/h3][p] [/p]

notes.title: Hermit Demo Limited Playtest - now available!
notes.content:
[p]Hello all!  [/p][h3][b]The Hermit Demo Limited Playtest is now available! You can request access today.[/b][/h3][p] It’s an exciting announcement today – the public playtest is now available. I will first be doing a limited playtest with a smaller sample of players (request access, then be granted access a few people at a time). As long as no major stability issues are reported, within the next few days I will be opening up the playtest fully so that you can immediately download and play without requesting access (open playtest).[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/93adda3b5072479b669c77c524e8924b30a4c387.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]
[b]What is this playtest?[/b][/h3][p]This is not a playtest of the whole game, but rather a playtest for the upcoming game demo which will be available on Steam sometime in the next couple of months.

I anticipate 4-6 hours of gameplay (it’s a big demo), but the game demo here is not part of the main game world. The game demo is actually its own, fully open-world, limited experience within the Hermit world. The playtest is for the Demo version 0.8.20, which is the current version of the game demo including most recent fixes/optimizations.

As the main purpose is to help me gather information about bugs/performance issues, the demo playtest features a bug reporting button on the main menu.[/p][p]Other than that, just enjoy this preview of the upcoming Hermit demo![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/e645e673d7a9da4cd42567682411a1a606e018dd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Known Issues:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The use of Torches and Bows is a bit cumbersome; while quick-throwing torches alleviates this somewhat, my intention for the full game release is that Bows, Torches, and Weapons will each have separate equipment slots on the Player Character loadout (which should make swapping between them significantly smoother)[/p][/*][*][p]Control remapping is currently still unavailable; you are still welcome to try the demo if you are from a region using non-QWERTY keyboard layouts but you may find this cumbersome without key remapping implemented (this is planned for future releases, but is not available yet)[/p][/*][*][p]FSR3.0 is Implemented, but DLSS and XeSS are unlikely to be implemented in the Demo’s first release version[/p][/*][*][p]Some known bugs with quests, combat, and donkey companion behaviour still exist and are being looked into[/p][/*][*][p]Donkey/AIs may fail to jump over retaining walls near roads sometimes[/p][/*][*][p]AIs may rarely become stuck inside of walls or other objects; this is a known issue but being looked into[/p][/*][*][p]There is a known issue with using L-Alt to free-look while climbing on ladders; I am investigating this and a fix should be out shortly[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3] [b]Thank you for your continued support of the project![/b][/h3]

notes.title: Development Newsletter: August Development Updates
notes.content:
[p]Hello, all! 

[b]It’s time to again share some new updates regarding game development! 
[/b]
This month I’m hard at work on developing and refining AI types and AI behaviours, as well as spending time on bug fixing and optimization for the upcoming free game demo that should hopefully be ready for release sometime in the next few weeks.[/p][h1]
[b]AI Behaviour & Difficulty Modes[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]In terms of AI behaviour, work has been underway for over a year on a ‘Smart NPC’ class that allows all AIs to have the same set of functional behaviours; all characters can be damaged or interacted with in similar ways. This means that characters in towns and cities don't just patrol a random loop, but instead have more compelling behaviour routines (storekeepers will stock shelves, roam their shop, wipe the tables, etc.) - and those same characters can also engage in combat, fleeing, etc.

Recent work has been heavily focused on adding dynamic difficulty scaling. Many games have rather uninteresting/disappointing systems for difficulty scaling (i.e., they simply scale up enemy HP/Damage). For Hermit, I wanted to ensure that NPCs feel harder without simply changing these parameters.

Harder difficulty modes should feel harder because of more intelligent AI behaviour rather than attributes. The new difficulty mode setting therefore changes some features of AI behaviour sequences to manage combat difficulty.
[/p][p][b]On harder difficulty modes:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]AIs are more likely to block or dodge[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]AIs are more likely to be able to heal[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]AIs are more likely to fix bleeds and fractures during combat[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]AIs strafe and approach more quickly[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]AIs attack faster and with less delay between strikes[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]The result is a change in the way combat feels rather than simply longer fights versus enemies with more HP. 

Since there are extremely tight time/budget constraints for Hermit (as a solo-developed project), these kinds of thoughtful design choices in game programming can make the world feel more alive without adding too much overhead.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/c6d03cbd869a48dcaa37d81ca6a2500fe940fdfc.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]Enemy NPC Types[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]One of the other areas of focus right now is on making sure that NPCs fit the world and behave in natural/interesting ways. All characters, including those that are not critical to the game's main story line (such as the Undead and other mobs), should clearly fit into the world in a natural way. Importantly, minor characters shouldn't just be 'generic filler NPCs' and instead should clearly belong to the places in the world where they are found.[/p][p]As a result, many types of combat NPCs (even simple ones like Skeletons) are being redesigned to ensure that they feel like they belong with their surroundings:[/p][list][*][p]Abandoned mines have undead miners[/p][/*][*][p]Ancient archives/libraries have undead librarians[/p][/*][*][p]Dungeons/catacombs have undead peasants and soldiers/guardsman[/p][/*][*][p]Dungeon kitchens have undead cooks/chefs[/p][/*][/list][p]The hopeful result of this is that AI characters will more diegetically ‘fit’ with the world giving everything a more cohesive feel.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/403734c571997a032fe9516b1167b5c053ae6f8a.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]Settings, Optimization, Bug fixes[/b][/h1][p][b]
[/b]Work continues on optimization and bug fixes in advance of the upcoming Free Game Demo to be released soon on Steam. More than 50 bugs have been fixed over the past two weeks and the game demo is approaching a level of stability and optimization now where it is almost ready to begin close beta testing.

Other recent developments in this category:[/p][list][*][p]Added separate world and music volume sliders[/p][/*][*][p]Added game difficulty settings to the settings menu[/p][/*][*][p]Added new settings for graphics scalability[/p][/*][*][p]Added new settings to enable/disable motion blur[/p][/*][*][p]Added new settings to enable/disable auto-hiding the hotkey bar[/p][/*][/list][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/b74a6f61eedc6ee6fa7ed675666f0d92ca51dd01.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]Known Issues[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]While significant work has been done on improving the game, there are still some areas where issues persist. Some of these are unlikely to be fixed before the initial Demo release, but are on the task list for the main game release.[/p][list][*][p]The use of Torches and Bows is a bit cumbersome; while quick-throwing torches alleviates this somewhat, my intention for the full game release is that Bows, Torches, and Weapons will each have separate equipment slots on the Player Character (which should make swapping between them significantly smoother)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]FSR3 is Implemented, but DLSS and XeSS are unlikely to be implemented in the Demo’s first release version[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Some known bugs with quests, combat, and donkey companion behaviour still exist and are being looked into[/p][/*][*][p]Control remapping is currently still unavailable[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/e89695679a78904bafcd8300b72c2e34fde9594e.png"][/img]
[b]Thank you for your continued support of the project![/b][/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Development Newsletter: Development Updates & Game Demo Announcement
notes.content:
[p]Hello all!

[b]I’d like to share some new updates regarding the game, development, and upcoming Demo![/b]

I’m currently hard at work on developing and refining the free game demo, which will hopefully be ready for release sometime in the next month or two. Right now, the main focus is on refining the spells, combat, and quests in advance of the demo, as well as on building out the major city and POIs for that release. Work on the main game is on a brief hiatus until after the demo release is ready.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Upcoming Game Demo[/b][/h1][p]Today I am announcing the release of the Hermit Demo Store Page (live now) for the upcoming Game Demo that I am hoping to release some time within the next couple of months. Stay tuned for more updates specifically about the game demo; the release date for that will be announced some time within the next few weeks. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/e7f7be87bf5b95dbd8df25f3163148989ed93d52.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1][b]Magic Mechanics[/b][/h1][p]Work continues on making magic and combat interesting. Two of the major design pillars for the game are that [b](1) magic and combat should feel great[/b], and that [b](2) spells should be dynamic and interact with/respond to the world around you[/b].[/p][p]Designing awesome spells requires a lot of programming work and testing. Over the past two months significant progress has been made towards creating Wind & Fire spells, as well as special conditional effects and combinations of those. Stay tuned for more updates on this as the spell trees will undergo significant upgrades/changes over the coming weeks and months.

Recent game updates on magic mechanics include:[/p][list][*][p]Spells that respond to the current weather[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Spells that respond to the time of day[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Spells that change the immediate environment in some way (such as creating obstacles or setting the ground on fire, burning/catching fire to NPCs that walk through the flames)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Spell classes that can be combined through crafting[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h1][b]Combat & Related Gameplay[/b][/h1][p]Weapon classes in Hermit are now balanced around parry-speed vs. stability, damage vs. versatility, and status effects. The past 8-12 months have seen significant work on combat mechanics, and major improvements have been made to AI combat abilities to ensure a smooth/functional (bug free) combat experience. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Large, heavy (2H) weapons:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Have long slow swings and are more difficult to parry attacks with[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Deal more health and stability damage to foes (causing stagger or knockdown)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Have a chance to break bones[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Cannot be used with a shield (required to block arrows)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Small, nimble (1H) weapons:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Are faster to attack with and easier to parry attacks with, but deal less damage per swing[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Have little effect on stability, meaning you’ll have to be able to parry incoming attacks in order to throw enemies off balance[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Have a chance to cause bleeds rather than fractures[/p][/*][*][p]Can be used with a shield[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Status Effects[/b][/h3][p]Updates in the past months have also included the addition of new status effects and other systems:[/p][list][*][p]Added Light and Heavy bleeds[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added fractures/broken bones (also integrated with fall damage)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added poison, toxins, diseases, and food-borne illness[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Add burning (can be extinguished by water or by rolling – stop, drop, and roll!)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Medical items (bandages, suturing kits, etc.) can now be found, crafted, or purchased, and they can be hotkeyed from an equipped pouch/satchel in order to quickly deal with combat-related status effects like bleeding[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h1][b]Ladders, Climbing, & Water[/b][/h1][p]This update includes several major improvements and bug fixes for ladders & climbable rocks/ledges as well.[/p][list][*][p]Added support for teleporting off of ladders, which could cause issues[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added support for transitioning to or from ladders directly into/out of water, which is required for the player to enter/exit boats from swimming[/p][/*][/list][p]These changes primarily reflect new infrastructure required to support more complex interactions/behaviours around ladders and climbing (the most importance of which are boats and water). [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/bdd1a927894f86bdfda24873b1b996b756564bc2.png"][/img][/p][p]While boats will not be finished in time for the game demo, the ocean buoyancy system is near completion and sailing is expected to be supported in some form for the initial release of the main game. With regards to oceans, rivers, and lakes, recent work includes the following updates:[/p][list][*][p]Finished work on the ocean, lake, and river water shaders[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work on ‘roiling boiling liquid’ (poisoned/toxic liquid) shaders[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work on the river spline system[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work on ocean Gerstner waves[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work on ocean and river buoyancy[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Made major progress towards finishing work on boats, ships, and sailing (buoyant propulsion and steering)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][b]NPC AI Development[/b][/h1][p]Work continues on a class of smart AIs that are performant and responsive. Most AI classes in the game have similar capabilities (for example, villager crowds can attack or flee much like enemies can). Since the game is expected to feature hundreds of NPCs, the most important consideration is game performance. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/d26be02d5b0236be4e38b10352b55e2bf017b3fe.png"][/img]New this month:[/p][list][*][p]Added new checks to AI death logic to prevent them from clipping through walls during death animations[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added new enemy AI classes with unique combat abilities[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Adjusted AI optimizations for the upcoming Demo[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work on AI work routines, allowing AIs to perform various actions in the world (stocking shelves, picking fruit, walking patrol routes, fishing, etc.) with the overall aim being to bring life to NPCs in the world[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished implementing AI work routines for NPCs throughout the demo world[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added sleep, eat, idle routines for farm animals like cows and pigs[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Finished work programming the new AI standings system, which allows AI groups to have hostility/friendliness with each other as well as the player (e.g., Wolves may chase deer but ignore foxes, and the player can become hostile with NPC groups by attacking or offending them)[b] [/b][/p][/*][/list][p][b] [/b][/p][h1][b]Performance & Optimizations[/b][/h1][p]I am continuing to refine and optimize game performance in advance of the Demo release. The target for performance in the game demo is 60FPS on minimum hardware requirements (RTX 3060 \[Desktop Version] or equivalent GPU), and it’s looking promising that this level of performance will be achievable using Unreal Engine 5.4 (with more significant improvements in render thread performance coming with Unreal Engine’s 5.6 release).

The game demo currently supports upscaling and frame interpolation using FSR3.0, but DLSS and Intel XESS implementations are still outstanding. Since FSR3.0 is hardware agnostic, this will likely remain the major upscaling method until after the demo release (with other upscalers being implemented for the full game release and possibly an update to the demo later on).[/p][p]Additional optimizations in this update include performance updates and other fixes to screen-space widgets for world interactables.[/p][list][*][p]Fixes to UI bugs that could cause interactable widgets to fail to disappear[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fixes to object interaction selection widget, removing bugs that could prevent the player from easily choosing which specific object (from several within range) they want to interact with[/p][/*][/list][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/2dfb96e84ac395df9b2aed799e51c5d32c052fab.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]Towns, Villages, & Cities[/b][/h1][p]For the main game release, the town of [b]Roshuridan[/b] was completed as the first major area in the game. A major feature of the game’s towns and villages is that almost every building in the game is enterable.

With the first major towns of the main game having already been completed and polished, the main focus is now on adapting one new town ([b]Gravenstaad[/b]) for the game demo. As a small-medium sized walled town, it makes for an interesting game location for players to explore during the demo without giving too much away for the real full game release.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/12a4be32c855472d82cb14c4100dcae68e7b1492.png"][/img][/p][p]As such, a modified, reduced-scale version of the city and surrounding area has been crafted specifically for the demo in order to provide a fun open-world experience while remaining a different/unique area from the real main game.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/882d04770763039b1d3f671adcfe62ceb76e11c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h1][b]Quests & UI[/b][/h1][p]One of the major gameplay hurdles to overcome during development is ensuring that the player cannot become stuck or lost. For quests requiring items, this means that dropping or losing those items could halt player progress and cause quest failure.[/p][p]The new quest journal features its own separate inventory space for quest items, preventing the accidental permanent loss of items required for game progression.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45654555/1fbec7bae79d8884361bcc4f9b7b99b45918d294.png"][/img][/p][h3]
[b]Thank you for your continued support of the project![/b][/h3][p] [/p]
